Key Research Thinking Patterns: Pattern Name: Adversarial Machine Learning (AML) Attack Formulation (This pattern involves integrating human perception models into attack formulations to create novel adversarial audios or signals that can evade detection by machine learning-based systems, as seen in the CEMF-PA attack against music copyright detection.)

Pattern Name: Comparative Analysis of Quantum and Classical Machine Learning (This pattern involves comparing the performance and security implications of quantum machine learning algorithms with their classical counterparts on real-world datasets, as seen in the study on Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.)

Pattern Name: Vulnerability Exploitation in Location-Based Services (This pattern involves identifying vulnerabilities in location-based services, such as the Google Geolocation API, and exploiting them to launch location spoofing attacks, as seen in the LLT inference attack.)

Pattern Name: Defense Against CSI-Based Attacks (This pattern involves developing defense schemes to counteract CSI-based attacks, such as breathing rate inference and crowd counting attacks, as seen in the HoneyBreath and Ghost defense schemes.)
Summary Description: Shangqing Zhao is a researcher with expertise in machine learning, quantum computing, and wireless security. Their work focuses on developing novel adversarial machine learning attacks and defenses, as well as exploring the performance and security implications of quantum machine learning algorithms. They have also investigated vulnerabilities in location-based services and developed defense schemes to counteract CSI-based attacks. Their research has applications in machine learning in real-world applications, wireless security, quantum security, healthcare, IoT, and inventory and logistics management.
